hints.title: Match Outcome Point System
hints.text: A team earns 3 points for a win, 1 point for a tie, and 0 for a loss, whether playing at home or away.

hints.title: Team Points Union and Left Join
hints.text: Generate point events for host and guest teams separately. Left join teams to points to preserve teams with 0 points.

hints.title: Team Scores Blueprint
hints.text: with MatchPoints as (select host_team as team_id, case when host_goals > guest_goals then 3 when host_goals = guest_goals then 1 else 0 end as points from Matches union all select guest_team as team_id, case when guest_goals > host_goals then 3 when guest_goals = host_goals then 1 else 0 end as points from Matches) select t.team_id, t.team_name, coalesce(sum(m.points), 0) as num_points from Teams t left join MatchPoints m on t.team_id = m.team_id group by t.team_id, t.team_name order by num_points desc, t.team_id asc.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH MatchPoints AS (
    SELECT host_team AS team_id,
           CASE 
               WHEN host_goals > guest_goals THEN 3
               WHEN host_goals = guest_goals THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END AS points
    FROM Matches
    UNION ALL
    SELECT guest_team AS team_id,
           CASE 
               WHEN guest_goals > host_goals THEN 3
               WHEN guest_goals = host_goals THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END AS points
    FROM Matches
)
SELECT t.team_id, t.team_name,
       COALESCE(SUM(m.points), 0) AS num_points
FROM Teams t
LEFT JOIN MatchPoints m ON t.team_id = m.team_id
GROUP BY t.team_id, t.team_name
ORDER BY num_points DESC, t.team_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Stacking host/guest points and sorting grouped teams runs in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner joining drops teams that never played a match or scored zero points.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Union all normalizes home and away perspectives into an indexable point stream.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of UNION ALL, LEFT JOIN to preserve 0-point teams, and ORDER BY num_points DESC, team_id ASC.

import pandas as pd

def team_scores(teams: pd.DataFrame, matches: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    p1 = []
    p2 = []
    for _, row in matches.iterrows():
        if row['host_goals'] > row['guest_goals']:
            p1.append({'team_id': row['host_team'], 'points': 3})
            p2.append({'team_id': row['guest_team'], 'points': 0})
        elif row['host_goals'] == row['guest_goals']:
            p1.append({'team_id': row['host_team'], 'points': 1})
            p2.append({'team_id': row['guest_team'], 'points': 1})
        else:
            p1.append({'team_id': row['host_team'], 'points': 0})
            p2.append({'team_id': row['guest_team'], 'points': 3})
    all_points = pd.DataFrame(p1 + p2)
    scores = all_points.groupby('team_id')['points'].sum().reset_index() if not all_points.empty else pd.DataFrame(columns=['team_id', 'points'])
    merged = teams.merge(scores, on='team_id', how='left')
    merged['num_points'] = merged['points'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return merged.sort_values(by=['num_points', 'team_id'], ascending=[False, True])[['team_id', 'team_name', 'num_points']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Row Point Evaluation and Outer Merge Sort
